19.title: GERMAN LESSON 14: German professions – Deutsche Berufe: Was sind Sie von Beruf?
19.focus: Note the male and female forms of each job and say the jobs aloud. Then say what you do: “Ich bin …”.

questions.q: How do you formally ask someone’s profession?
What is the female form of “der Lehrer”?
How do you say “I am a teacher” (female)?
questions.why: Professions normally have no article after sein.

20.title: Learn German | German Grammar | Dative case | Dativ | A1
20.focus: Watch how the articles change in the dative and which question word finds the dative object. Pause and repeat each example sentence.

questions.q: Which question word asks for the dative object?
questions.why: Wem gebe ich das Buch? – dem Mann.

questions.q: Ich gebe ___ Mann das Buch. (der Mann, dative)
Which preposition always takes the dative?
questions.why: mit dem Bus, mit der Bahn.

21.title: How to Give Directions in German | Super Easy German 185
21.focus: Follow the route on the map while you listen. Collect every direction word: geradeaus, links, rechts, die Straße, die Ampel.

o: How do I get to the station?

22.title: An EASY explanation of the 9 Two-Way PREPOSITIONS (Wechselpräpositionen)
22.focus: Learn the nine prepositions, then the one trick: wo? = dative (position), wohin? = accusative (movement).

questions.q: How many two-way prepositions does German have?
questions.why: an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, zwischen.

questions.q: Which case follows a two-way preposition when you answer “Wohin?” (movement)?
Das Buch liegt auf ___ Tisch. (der Tisch, wo?)

23.title: GERMAN LESSON 27: Learn German Vocabulary of FOOD (Das Essen)
23.focus: Write each food word with its article. Repeat aloud and say which foods you like.

o: When you arrive at a hotel
questions.why: It is the wish for a good meal.

24.title: Hoch, höher am höchsten! (German Comparative)
24.focus: Note how the comparative ends in -er and the superlative in am … -sten, and which vowels get an umlaut.

25.title: Grocery shopping in German | Super Easy German (33)
25.focus: Listen to real shop conversations. Notice how people ask for quantities and how the shop assistant asks “Sonst noch etwas?”.

questions.q: Who usually says “Was darf es sein?”
questions.why: It means: What can I get you?

questions.q: “Ich hätte gern ein Kilo Äpfel.” means:
o: I would like a kilo of apples.
I have a kilo of apples.
questions.why: Ich hätte gern = I would like.

26.title: Imperatives: How to Phrase Orders and Requests in German
26.focus: Compare the three imperative forms (du, ihr, Sie) and the politeness words bitte and mal.

questions.why: Remove -st from the du-form: du kommst → Komm!

questions.q: What is the formal imperative of “kommen”?

27.title: Understand the German Perfect! (Only in German) – Das deutsche Perfekt
27.focus: Anja explains the Perfekt in German only. Listen for haben/sein and the Partizip II at the end of the sentence.

questions.why: Ich habe gegessen. Ich bin gefahren.

questions.q: Where does the Partizip II stand in a main clause?

28.title: Perfekt mit SEIN: When to use the German PERFECT Tense with “to Be”
28.focus: List the two groups of verbs that take sein: movement (gehen, fahren, fliegen) and change of state (aufwachen, werden), plus sein and bleiben.

questions.q: Which verbs typically form the Perfekt with sein?
o: Verbs of movement and change of state
questions.why: Ich bin gefahren, ich bin aufgewacht.

questions.q: What is the Partizip II of “gehen”?

29.title: Learn German Vocabulary – Weather in German (Wetter)
29.focus: Repeat each weather expression aloud, then say what the weather is like where you are today.

30.title: German Clothing Vocabulary
30.focus: Note the gender of every item of clothing, and which items are always plural (die Schuhe, die Socken, die Jeans).

questions.q: Which article goes with the plural “Schuhe”?

31.title: A1 – Lesson 25 | the family in German | die Familie | Meine Familie
31.focus: Build the family tree with the German words and say sentences: Das ist mein Bruder. Meine Mutter heißt …

questions.q: Meine Mutter und mein Vater sind meine ___. (parents)

32.title: The ACCUSATIVE Part 4: German MICH, DICH, EUCH, … Personal Pronouns of the accusative
32.focus: Write the full table: mich, dich, ihn, sie, es, uns, euch, sie/Sie. Then make one sentence for each.

questions.q: Which case are mich, dich, ihn, sie, es in?

33.title: Sports in Slow German
33.focus: Listen to the slow German and note the sports, the verbs (spielen, machen, gehen) and how often people exercise.

questions.q: How do you say “I play tennis”?

34.title: How Do Germans Stay in Shape? | Easy German 424
34.focus: Street interviews about sport and fitness. Turn on the German subtitles, and note how people answer “Machst du Sport?”.

questions.q: “Wie oft machst du Sport?” asks about:

35.title: A1 – Lesson 59 | Beim Arzt | At the Doctor’s | Arzttermin vereinbaren
35.focus: Follow the dialogues: making an appointment, describing pain, and the doctor’s advice. Repeat the key sentences.

o: I would like to make an appointment.
I would like to cancel my visit.

36.title: Don’t Mix Up “seit”, “für” & “vor”! (German Temporal Prepositions)
36.focus: Compare the three prepositions: seit (since, still going on), für (for a planned length), vor (ago).

questions.q: “Ich wohne seit zwei Jahren in Berlin.” means:
o: I have been living in Berlin for two years (and still do).
I lived in Berlin two years ago.
I will live in Berlin for two years.
questions.why: seit + dative + present tense = since/for until now.
seit einem Jahr = for a year now.

37.title: THE DATIVE part 3: Mir, dir, Ihnen in GERMAN – Personal Pronouns in the DATIVE
37.focus: Write the table mir, dir, ihm, ihr, ihm, uns, euch, ihnen, Ihnen and make a sentence with each.

questions.why: geben takes the dative for the person.

questions.q: What is the formal dative of “you”?

38.title: Subjunctive 2 with “hätten” & “wären” – 3 Minuten Deutsch #68
38.source: YouTube · Learn German with Herr Antrim
38.focus: Note how hätte and wäre express wishes and polite requests. Use them to finish the sentences: Ich hätte gern … Ich wäre gern …

questions.why: hätte gern = would like to have.

o: I would like to be rich.

questions.q: Ich ___ gern ein Haus. (haben, polite wish)
